attempts.summary: On node1 (Alpine 3.23), built a local apk package repository from packages fetched to local storage (musl, tree), served it via a persistent darkhttpd OpenRC service on $NODE_IP:8080 backed by /var/www/localhost/htdocs/localrepo. Simulated the usual remote repositories (dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org) being unreachable via a hosts-file DNS sinkhole, proved the remote was unreachable with curl (connection refused), then installed the `tree` package purely from the local HTTP repo while remote repos returned connection-refused errors. Verified the package is genuinely functional (tree v2.2.1 binary runs). Cleaned up the DNS sinkhole afterward to restore normal connectivity, leaving the local repo (with remote fallback) permanently configured. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and service/data health, issued a background `reboot` so the ack returned before disconnection, polled node1 until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed (82a04a58... -> a0d41fb7...) and boot time reset, and verified post-restart that the darkhttpd service auto-started, the local repo is served, tree remains installed, and apk update still shows the local repo reachable and remote repos unreachable-but-listed (real internet access was restored, confirmed working, before restart).
